Key Message 1...Isolated showers and thunderstorms today 
will be followed by dry weather tonight through Tuesday.

Cyclonic W'erly flow aloft and embedded shortwave troughs impact
Western and Central NY through this early evening. At the
surface, a cold front was located just east of Barrie, ON, just
west of Hamilton, ON, and extended generally S'ward across 
central Lake Erie at 2:20 AM EDT this morning. This front should 
sweep E'ward across our CWA between about 3 AM and 1 PM EDT 
today. Ahead of and behind the front, subtle surface trough 
axes attendant to the shortwave troughs aloft will traverse 
Western and Central NY generally from west to east. In addition,
behind the front, a surface ridge will build slowly from the 
Upper Midwest and vicinity. Isolated and periodic showers and 
thunderstorms are expected through this early evening as low-level
convergence and moist ascent along the cold front and surface 
trough axes release weak boundary layer CAPE. However, the 
threat for these showers and storms should end gradually and 
generally from west to east late this morning through early 
evening as the building surface ridge is accompanied by a 
lowering, strengthening, and stabilizing subsidence inversion. 
Lows should reach the 60's around daybreak this morning. Highs 
should reach the 70's to lower 80's late this afternoon, behind 
the weak cold front and amidst partly to mostly cloudy sky.

The high pressure ridge at the surface and aloft will build 
from the western Great Lakes and vicinity tonight through 
Tuesday. Stabilizing subsidence accompanying the ridge is 
expected to promote dry weather. Considerable clearing and weak 
or calm surface winds accompanying the ridge should contribute 
to lows reaching the 50's to lower 60's around daybreak Tuesday.
Steam fog should form in the river and lake valleys of the 
Western Southern Tier, Finger Lakes, and Eastern Lake Ontario 
Region late this evening and especially during the predawn hours
of Tuesday morning. Patchy radiation fog should also form 
during the same time period, especially inland from Lakes Erie 
and Ontario, amidst lingering low-level moisture from recent 
rainfall. Fog will dissipate via the onset of diurnal convective
mixing of the boundary layer shortly after daybreak. Highs are 
forecast to reach the 70's to lower 80's late Tuesday afternoon.

Key Message 2...Another round of isolated to scattered showers and 
thunderstorms is forecast for the midweek period.

The above-mentioned ridge at the surface and aloft exits E'ward
Tuesday night and allows a warm front to sweep N'ward through
Western and Central NY. Simultaneously, cyclonic W'erly flow
aloft becomes established over our area and embedded shortwave
disturbances traverse Western and Central NY. The cyclonic 
W'erly flow aloft and embedded shortwave disturbances should 
continue to affect our area on Wednesday, when a cold front
should sweep SE'ward through Western and Central NY. Isolated 
to scattered showers and thunderstorms are expected after 
midnight Tuesday night through Wednesday as weak to perhaps 
moderate CAPE, included elevated CAPE, is released by the 
following: moist isentropic ascent along the upper-reaches of 
the warm front and ahead of shortwave trough axes; low-level 
convergence and moist ascent along the surface warm front, 
surface cold front, and surface trough axes attendant to the 
shortwave troughs. Overnight lows should reach mainly the mid 
50's to mid 60's Tuesday night and be followed by daytime highs 
in the 70's to 80F on Wednesday. 

During Wednesday night through Thursday, a ridge at the surface
and aloft is expected to build from the western Great Lakes and
vicinity. Primarily fair weather is expected in Western and
Central NY as stabilizing subsidence accompanies the ridge.
However, a few rain showers associated with moist isentropic 
ascent along the upper-reaches of the departing cold front may 
impact the Western Southern Tier and southern Finger Lakes 
Wednesday evening. Latest trends in NWP model guidance suggest 
the cooler air mass behind the cold front may be too dry and not
cold enough to support a period of lake-effect rain. Overnight 
lows should reach the upper 40's to near 60F around daybreak 
Thursday as the cooler air mass overspreads our region behind 
the cold front. Highs should reach the 70's late Thursday 
afternoon.
